# How to Use Shopify Customer Events for Tracking

[Shopify](https://stape.io/blog/category/shopify)

Shopify Customer Events explained & setup guide
===============================================

![Tymofii Sankov](https://stape.io/cdn-cgi/image/width=96/https://cdn.stape.io/i/67fe40f9e688d734138010.png)

Tymofii Sankov

Author

Published

Sep 15, 2026

comments

[Join the conversation](https://stape.io/blog/shopify-customer-events#comments)

i

Key takeaways:

*   **Shopify Customer Events provide structured data on customer interactions** across the storefront and checkout, which pixels can use for analytics and advertising.
    
*   **Standard events cover common eCommerce actions**, while custom events extend the setup for tracking store-specific interactions.
    
*   **Customer Events can work with both app and custom pixels**, and you can integrate them with Google Tag Manager to manage tracking across multiple platforms.
    
*   **Customer Events provide interaction data, while** [**server-side tracking**](https://stape.io/blog/server-side-tagging-for-shopify)
     **gives you more control** over how this data is processed and delivered to analytics and advertising platforms.
    

Shopify merchants rely on customer data to understand how visitors interact with their stores and measure the performance of their marketing campaigns. However, collecting this data is becoming more challenging as traditional tracking signals disappear. Official statistics show that [95% of advertising and data decision-makers expect continued signal loss](https://www.shopify.com/blog/ecommerce-data-analytics)
, including identifiers such as third-party cookies and device IDs. Shopify Customer Events offer a framework for working with customer activity, considering the new specifics. In this guide, we'll take a closer look at this functionality, its setup, and its role in your tracking infrastructure.

What are Shopify Customer Events?
---------------------------------

An event in the Shopify ecosystem is a customer's action taken at any stage of their journey. These events turn all interactions into structured data checkpoints that describe, step by step, what is happening in your store.

Before this system was introduced, all the tracking was done manually through the code. Customer events enabled shop owners to minimize manual work by connecting to the Customer Events Framework, which provides more accurate, structured event data. Roughly speaking, Customer Events can be divided into two types:

*   **Shopify standard events** are predefined and cover common customer interactions across the storefront and checkout: `page_viewed`, `product_viewed`, `product_added_to_cart`, `checkout_completed`, etc.
    
*   **Custom events** are needed when there is no standard event available for the type of interaction you want to track specifically for your project.
    

Roughly speaking, all standard events are Customer Events, but not all Customer Events are standard. We will cover both types and their differences later in this guide, so do not panic yet. Things are simpler than they seem.

Data gathered through this framework can be later used for advertising, analytics, and other marketing purposes. However, it is important to clarify that Customer Events do not do analytics or advertising on their own. To understand their role in data tracking, let's first dissect how they work.

### How Shopify Customer Events work

The basic logic behind Customer Events is quite straightforward. When a customer performs an action in your store, Shopify identifies it and pushes a corresponding event. A connected pixel can then use the event data and send the required information to an analytics or advertising platform. 

![Shopify Customer Events workflow](https://stape.io/cdn-cgi/image/width=3840/https://cdn.stape.io/i/6aa8f5ceed816363759638.png)

Other customer actions covered by standard events, such as adding to cart and completing a purchase, are recorded in the same way, providing a consistent structure for the collected data. This means you do not need to set up a separate mechanism to detect the same customer actions on every third-party platform you work with. 

Shopify standard events: full reference list
--------------------------------------------

Shopify has a set of [predefined standard events](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/web-pixels-api/standard-events)
 that cover the main customer interactions with your store across the storefront and checkout. Each event corresponds to a specific action, such as viewing a product, starting checkout, or completing a purchase. This gives you a ready-to-use set of events for tracking the most important stages of the customer journey. 

| **Event name** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `_alert_displayed_` | Alert message, alert type, affected field/target, and its value |
| `_cart_viewed_` | Cart contents, quantities, estimated costs, and cart attributes |
| `_checkout_address_info_submitted_` | Checkout information, including available billing/shipping address and checkout details |
| `_checkout_completed_` | Checkout and purchase information, including products, totals, discounts, shipping, and transaction details |
| `_checkout_contact_info_submitted_` | Checkout information, including available customer contact and checkout details |
| `_checkout_shipping_info_submitted_` | Checkout information, including shipping and delivery details |
| `_checkout_started_` | Checkout information, including products, prices, discounts, and available customer details |
| `_collection_viewed_` | Collection information and the product variants included in the collection |
| `_page_viewed_` | No additional event-specific data; page information such as URL and title is available through the event context |
| `_payment_info_submitted_` | Checkout information associated with the payment step |
| `_product_added_to_cart_` | Added product/variant, quantity, and line cost |
| `_product_removed_from_cart_` | Removed product/variant, quantity, and line cost |
| `_product_viewed_` | Product variant information, including product details |
| `_search_submitted_` | Search query and product variants returned by the search |

This set of events covers most basic customer interactions typically tracked in eCommerce analytics and advertising. They are called standard events because Shopify automatically creates and recognizes them for common customer actions, using a consistent naming convention and data structure. However, some stores may have specific tracking requirements that are not covered by this standard set. In such cases, custom events can be created to track additional interactions. 

Standard events vs. custom events
---------------------------------

Let's say that your store has a configurator that allows customers to create a product based on their own needs and requirements (e.g., table length, width, height, color, etc.). You want to track how many customers complete the configuration and proceed to purchase, but there is no standard event that captures this interaction. In this case, you can create a custom event and configure which information it should include when triggered. The main difference here is the level of control you have over the event:

*   you can create an understandable name based on the type of interaction you track;
    
*   you can define exactly when the event is published;
    
*   you can specify what data is included in the event.
    

Once you publish the custom event, a pixel can subscribe to it in the same way it does to standard events and use its data for analytics or advertising. This way, you can extend the basic set of Shopify events to meet your specific tracking needs.

IMPORTANT!

Custom events do not replace the standard set. You can use both together, and if a standard event already covers the interaction you need, there is usually no reason to create a custom one. Consider custom events as additional flexibility for specific tracking requirements rather than a must-have for every Shopify store.

Shopify app pixels vs. custom pixels
------------------------------------

Shopify allows you to work with Customer Events through two types of pixels: **app pixels and custom pixels**. Both can access Customer Events and use their data for tracking, but the practical difference lies in how they are added, configured, and maintained.

**App pixels** are provided through Shopify apps and built by app developers using the Web Pixels API. From a store owner's perspective, most of the technical implementation and maintenance happen on the developer's side. You install and configure the corresponding app, while its pixel handles the supported tracking functionality in the background.

**Custom pixels** let you add your own code via the Customer Events section in Shopify. This provides greater control over the implementation and allows you to adapt tracking to your specific requirements. At the same time, setting up and maintaining a custom pixel usually requires more technical knowledge.

|     | **App pixels** | **Custom pixels** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Setup** | Is added automatically by a Shopify app | Code is added manually through Customer Events |
| **Technical knowledge** | Usually minimal | It is best to have JavaScript knowledge and a basic understanding of how tracking happens |
| **Control** | Depends on the app's functionality | Greater control over implementation |
| **Maintainance** | Is primarily handled on the app developer’s side | Managed on your side as a part of your tracking setup |
| **Best for** | Fast integrations via Shopify apps | Custom integrations and specific tracking requirements |

In practice, this does not mean that you need to choose one over the other. If you have specific tracking requirements, app and custom pixels can coexist in the same store. Moreover, custom pixels can also be used in more advanced tracking setups that combine Shopify Customer Events with Google Tag Manager and server-side tracking, which we will discuss later in this article.

How to set up Shopify Customer Events
-------------------------------------

There is no Customer Events Shopify activation button in your store settings. The platform automatically publishes standard events, and your task is to configure how you want to use this data.

### Option 1: use an app pixel

If you have decided to use an app pixel, start by finding the required integration in the Shopify App Store. For example, you can connect your store to platforms such as [Meta](https://apps.shopify.com/facebook)
 and [Google](https://apps.shopify.com/google)
 through their Shopify integrations, including setups for tracking Shopify Facebook pixel events. The exact setup depends on the app, but the general process looks like this:

1.  Install the required app from the Shopify App Store.
    
2.  Give the app the required permissions.
    
3.  Connect your advertising or analytics account.
    
4.  Configure the available tracking settings according to your needs.
    
5.  Test the integration to ensure the required events are recorded.
    

The main advantage of this approach is that the app handles the pixel implementation and maintenance, so you do not need to work with its code manually.

### Option 2: add a custom pixel

For a custom implementation, you first need the pixel script for the tracking solution you want to connect. Shopify provides the environment where you can add and manage a custom pixel, but the script itself is your responsibility; if you have it already, follow the steps below.

1\. In your Shopify admin, open **Settings** → **Customer events**.

![Customer events in Shopify](https://stape.io/cdn-cgi/image/width=3840/https://cdn.stape.io/i/6aa917da06dc3290947824.png)

2\. Click **Add custom pixel**, give it an identifiable name, and click **Add pixel**.

![Add custom pixel popup](https://stape.io/cdn-cgi/image/width=3840/https://cdn.stape.io/i/6aa919e418868518370758.png)

3\. Paste the provided code into the custom pixel editor.

![Code in the custom pixel editor](https://stape.io/cdn-cgi/image/width=3840/https://cdn.stape.io/i/6aa91a1ebab0e564637510.png)

4\. Review and configure the available customer privacy settings according to your tracking setup and consent requirements.

5\. Click **Save** at the top and then **Connect** to activate the pixel.

![Connected pixel](https://stape.io/cdn-cgi/image/width=3840/https://cdn.stape.io/i/6aa91a8117df3906526085.png)

6\. Perform the customer actions you want to track, and verify that the expected events and data reach their destinations.

Once connected, the custom pixel can subscribe to the Shopify Customer Events specified in its code and use their data for the tracking implementation it was created for. 

How to use Shopify Customer Events with Google Tag Manager
----------------------------------------------------------

Google Tag Manager is not required to use Shopify Customer Events. A pixel can send collected data directly to an analytics or advertising platform. However, if you work with several platforms or already manage your tracking through GTM, adding it to the setup can make the whole process easier to manage.

### How Shopify Customer Events work with GTM

In this setup, GTM sits between the data collected from your Shopify store and the analytics or advertising platforms where you want to use it. The general flow looks like this:

**Customer action → Shopify Customer Event → Custom pixel → Data Layer → Google Tag Manager → Analytics and advertising platforms**

The custom pixel subscribes to the required Shopify pixel events and makes its data available to your tracking setup through the Data Layer. GTM can then use this information to trigger the appropriate tags and send the required data to [GA4](https://stape.io/blog/shopify-google-analytics-4-tracking)
, [Google Ads](https://stape.io/blog/server-side-google-ads-conversion-tracking-in-shopify)
, [Meta](https://stape.io/blog/facebook-conversion-api-and-shopify)
, or other platforms.

You can build this connection manually if you have enough technical knowledge to correctly subscribe to the events, structure their data, and make it available to GTM. Alternatively, you can use the [Stape Conversion Tracking app](https://stape.io/solutions/shopify-app)
 to simplify the process. The app can generate the custom pixel needed to create [eCommerce Data Layer](https://stape.io/blog/shopify-data-layer)
 events and add your web GTM container to the Shopify store. The general setup looks like this:

1.  Install the Stape Conversion Tracking app and add your web GTM container ID.
    
2.  Enable the eCommerce Data Layer functionality in the app.
    
3.  Copy the generated custom pixel code.
    
4.  In Shopify, go to **Settings → Customer events → Add custom pixel**.
    
5.  Paste the generated code, save it, and connect the pixel.
    
6.  Test the setup to verify that the expected eCommerce events are available in GTM.
    

Once the connection is working, you can configure the required tags, triggers, and variables in GTM to work with the needed platforms.

### Why use GTM with Shopify Customer Events?

Adding GTM gives you more control over how Shopify Customer Events are used after they are collected. This provides several practical benefits:

*   **Centralized tracking management:** manage tags for GA4, Google Ads, Meta, and other platforms from the same GTM container.
    
*   **Greater flexibility:** control which events activate particular tags and what information is sent to each destination.
    
*   **Easier updates:** make many tracking changes in GTM without modifying your Shopify custom pixel each time.
    

This makes GTM especially useful as your tracking setup grows and you start working with more platforms. At the same time, the flexibility of such a setup makes correct configuration and testing particularly important.

Common Shopify Customer Events mistakes
---------------------------------------

Shopify Customer Events simplify access to customer activity data, but the quality of your tracking still depends on how you configure and use them. Here are some common mistakes to avoid.

### Creating unnecessary custom events

If Shopify already provides a standard event for the interaction you need to track, there is usually no reason to recreate it as a custom event. Doing so adds unnecessary complexity and makes your tracking setup harder to manage.

### Tracking the same event through multiple integrations

App pixels, custom pixels, and GTM can coexist in the same store, but you need to make sure they do not send the same event to the same platform twice. For example, tracking a purchase through both an app integration and GTM may result in duplicate conversions and inaccurate reporting.

### Ignoring customer privacy settings

When configuring pixels, consider what data they collect and when they are allowed to operate based on your customer privacy settings and applicable consent requirements. Connecting a pixel alone does not mean that every event should always be sent.

### Skipping testing after setup

A connected pixel does not necessarily mean that everything works correctly. Test the main customer actions in your store, such as viewing a product, adding it to the cart, starting checkout, and completing a purchase. Then verify that the expected events and data reach the intended platforms. [Stape's Chrome Extension](https://stape.io/solutions/stape-gtm-helper)
 can simplify this process by providing a more convenient way to inspect and debug your tracking setup.  

It is always better to take several extra checks and steps during the configuration and testing to avoid getting incorrect or duplicated data affecting your analytics later. If you face any issues at a later stage, check our [debugging guide](https://stape.io/blog/shopify-tracking-debugging-guide)
.

How Shopify Customer Events work with server-side tracking
----------------------------------------------------------

It is essential to distinguish here that Shopify Customer Events and server-side tracking are not alternatives. Customer Events provide information about interactions, while server-side tracking changes how this data is processed and delivered to analytics and advertising platforms.

When tracking requests are sent directly from the user's browser to platforms such as GA4, Google Ads, or Meta, they remain affected by ad blockers, browser restrictions, and network issues. Server-side tracking adds another layer to the process. If you extend the GTM setup described above with server-side tracking, the flow looks like this:

**Customer action → Shopify Customer Event → Custom pixel → GTM → Server GTM → Analytics and advertising platforms**

This approach can help you:

*   **reduce data loss** associated with browser-side tracking;
    
*   **control data before it is sent** by validating, modifying, or enriching it;
    
*   **manage data distribution** to different platforms from the server container.
    

The Stape Conversion Tracking app can connect the Shopify eCommerce events discussed earlier with your GTM setup. You can then extend this architecture with a [server GTM container hosted on Stape](https://stape.io/gtm-server-hosting)
, combining Shopify Customer Events with server-side tracking in the same setup.

Learn more about the [benefits of server-side tracking](https://stape.io/blog/benefits-server-side-tagging)
 and why it may be worth switching to it if you haven't done this yet.

Conclusion
----------

Shopify Customer Events provide a unified foundation for tracking customer interactions across your store. For many businesses, standard events and available app integrations, such as a native [Shopify GA4 integration](https://stape.io/blog/google-tag-manager-shopify-set-up)
, may already cover essential tracking needs, while custom events and pixels allow the setup to scale to meet more specific requirements. The important part is not to make tracking more complex than necessary, but to choose an implementation that matches the platforms you use and the data you actually need. As your requirements expand, Customer Events can also be integrated into a broader setup with Google Tag Manager and server-side tracking, giving you more control over your marketing and analytics data.

# Server-Side Tracking Is Easier Than You Think: Myths Busted

[sGTM hosting](https://stape.io/blog/category/sgtm-hosting)
[Stape features](https://stape.io/blog/category/stape-features)

Server-side tracking myths busted: what you actually need to know
=================================================================

![Tymofii Sankov](https://stape.io/cdn-cgi/image/width=96/https://cdn.stape.io/i/67fe40f9e688d734138010.png)

Tymofii Sankov

Author

Published

Sep 4, 2026

comments

[Join the conversation](https://stape.io/blog/server-side-tracking-myths#comments)

i

Key takeaways:

*   **Server-side tracking is accessible and beneficial to businesses of all sizes and budgets.** Stape allows you to try it for free and scale your setup whenever your needs grow.
    
*   **Implementation is easy.** Managed infrastructure, Setup Wizard, Tracking Checker, and other Stape tools reduce the amount of manual work needed.
    
*   **Server-side tracking provides more accurate and reliable data.** It helps reduce data loss caused by ad blockers, cookie limitations, browser restrictions, and other factors.
    
*   **It does not require constant manual maintenance.** Once configured, it does not need regular manual intervention. Stape further reduces the maintenance burden by managing the infrastructure, providing 24/7 SRE monitoring, and offering a vast toolkit that simplifies ongoing tracking management.
    

It is not the first year server-side tracking has been with us. It has already been quite some time, and yet many businesses still hesitate to implement it, despite its undoubted benefits. The main obstacles often mentioned as reasons are that server-side tracking is expensive, hard to configure, requires constant maintenance, is not as effective as it is viewed, etc. Of course, no smoke exists without fire, and most of these "accusations" WERE valid. Time passes, the technology improves, and what used to require significant resources for questionable functionality can now be much more effective and affordable.

In this article, we will take a closer look at four common server-side tracking myths, explain where they come from, and see how well they hold up in practice.

Server-side tracking is more affordable than many people think
--------------------------------------------------------------

![Server-side tracking cost](https://stape.io/cdn-cgi/image/width=3840/https://cdn.stape.io/i/6a9a754915704177775045.png)

Let's start with one of the most common concerns about [server-side tracking](http://stape.io/)
: cost. Server-side tracking uses server infrastructure to process incoming requests, so a new hosting element is added compared to the traditional client-side tracking setup. If you use a cloud provider like Google Cloud Platform for hosting, the final cost heavily depends on the infrastructure complexity and required resources.

This is where Stape makes a significant difference. We take an alternative approach, combining the required infrastructure with a vast toolkit developed specifically for server-side tracking. You can start with a free plan and move through the available tiers as your business expands, traffic grows, and requirements become more complex.

To make things even more transparent, we have a convenient [pricing calculator](https://stape.io/price)
 that would allow you to plan your spending and predict costs associated with your server-side tracking config. You enter the number of expected monthly events, what other tools you want to use, and see how much it will cost your business.

If you already invest significantly in paid advertising, even a tiny improvement can outweigh the monthly cost of server-side tracking. The ability to start with Stape at $0 and scale up together with your business according to your needs also helps to keep your spending proportional to your requirements.

After implementing server-side tracking with Stape, [SportSpar reduced its cost per purchase by 24% and increased ROAS by 32%](https://stape.io/blog/zweridigital-with-sportspar-got-24-cost-reduction-and-32-improvement-of-roas)
, providing a clear example of how improved tracking can translate into measurable advertising performance.

Server-side tracking can be implemented quickly and almost effortlessly
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

![Instant server-side tracking implementation](https://stape.io/cdn-cgi/image/width=3840/https://cdn.stape.io/i/6a9a754939eea047486792.png)

The word "server" makes the overall term "server-side tracking" sound more technical than it actually is. In fact, the amount of technical work to do heavily depends on the implementation method you choose.

If you decide to use Stape, for instance, we will manage all the infrastructure and hosting without requiring any involvement from your side. This way, you can focus solely on the server container, configuring the tags and destinations you need. If you have already worked with Google Tag Manager when setting up client-side tracking, many things will already be familiar to you.

Apart from taking care of the infrastructure and hosting, Stape also has numerous integrations and tools aimed at simplifying different aspects of implementation.

*   [**Setup Wizard**](https://stape.io/gtm-set-up-assistant)
    **.** Instead of manually creating tags, triggers, clients, and variables for every platform, you answer a short questionnaire, select your CMS and tracking destinations, and provide the necessary IDs and tokens. Setup Wizard then generates personalized web and server GTM container templates and can import them into GTM automatically.
    
*   **Free** [**CMS**](https://stape.io/helpdesk/documentation/integrations)
     **and** [**CRM**](https://stape.io/helpdesk/documentation/crm-apps)
     **integrations.** Stape offers apps, plugins, and extensions for popular platforms, including [Shopify](https://stape.io/solutions/shopify-app)
    , [WordPress](https://stape.io/solutions/server-side-tracking-for-wordpress)
    , [Magento 2](https://stape.io/solutions/gtm-server-side-extension-for-magento-2)
    , [BigCommerce](https://stape.io/solutions/stape-server-gtm-app-for-bigcommerce)
    , [Wix](https://stape.io/solutions/wix-app)
    , [PrestaShop](https://stape.io/solutions/prestashop-module)
    , and [Salla](https://stape.io/solutions/salla-app)
    . They automate parts of the setup that would otherwise require manual configuration, such as enriching the data layer, sending eCommerce events, or connecting sales data with advertising platforms.
    
*   [**AI Assistant**](https://stape.io/helpdesk/documentation/how-to-use-ai-assistant)
    **.** Stape's AI Assistant can interact with the Stape ecosystem and connect Google services using natural-language prompts. Among other supported tasks, it can analyze GA4 data and GTM containers and create, modify, or delete variables and templates in Google Tag Manager. 
    
*   [**Website Tracking Checker**](https://stape.io/website-tracking-checker)
    **.** Analyze your website's current tracking setup and identify potential weak points that may contribute to lost conversion data or inaccurate measurement. The tool does not modify your setup automatically; instead, it highlights areas that deserve attention and may benefit from improvement.
    

The exact implementation ultimately depends on the website and tracking requirements. A standard implementation can be covered almost solely by Stape, while a heavily customized setup may require slightly more involvement from your side. Either way, you do not have to build the server infrastructure from scratch yourself.

Server-side tracking is much more effective than a pure browser-based setup
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

![Server-side vs client-side tracking effectiveness](https://stape.io/cdn-cgi/image/width=3840/https://cdn.stape.io/i/6a9a75490c64d810733854.png)

The larger your advertising budget, the more you may be losing by relying solely on [client-side tracking](https://stape.io/blog/server-side-tagging-versus-client-side-tagging)
. In some cases, those losses can easily outweigh the cost of implementing server-side tracking. But why is that?

Сlient-side tracking can miss conversions due to ad blockers, browser restrictions, cookie limitations, and other factors. When some conversions and user interactions never reach your analytics and advertising platforms, campaign decisions are made using an incomplete picture of customer behavior. Over time, this can affect attribution, optimization, and ultimately the efficiency with which your advertising budget is spent.

Server-side tracking helps mitigate many of these issues by introducing an additional processing layer between your website and the platforms receiving your data. This gives you greater control over the information being collected, allowing you to enrich, validate, and refine events before they are sent to analytics and advertising platforms, which can improve conversion tracking. For instance, Google reports that Square saw [almost a 50% increase in conversion measurement](https://marketingplatform.google.com/about/resources/square-improves-conversion-measurement-securely-with-server-side-tagging/)
 with the implementation of server-side tracking.

As a result, campaign optimization is based on more complete and reliable data. Moreover, once your server container is running, you can extend its functionality with Stape's [power-ups](https://stape.io/solutions/category/power-ups)
 and [built-in features](https://stape.io/solutions/category/stape-benefits)
 designed specifically for server-side tracking. Depending on the feature and plan, these can help reduce data loss, improve data quality, extend cookie lifetime, enrich or transform incoming data, filter unwanted traffic, and automate particular tracking processes. For many businesses, all these improvements can translate into measurable changes in overall marketing performance, including [CPA reductions of up to 20%](https://stape.io/blog/herzlack-meta-tracking-optimization)
. 

What's more, you don't have to rely on assumptions to evaluate the impact. [Stape Analytics](https://stape.io/solutions/stape-analytics)
 measures the uplift after server-side tracking is implemented, allowing you to [compare your tracking before and after](https://stape.io/blog/sgtm-seoplus-marketing-measurement)
 the migration and see how it affects your data quality.

A good example comes from ZweiDigital, an agency specializing in performance marketing. After the agency migrated SportSpar’s tracking to Stape’s server-side configuration, [a 24% reduction in CPP and a 32% ROAS improvement](https://stape.io/blog/zweridigital-with-sportspar-got-24-cost-reduction-and-32-improvement-of-roas)
 were observed. Moreover, this switch boosted EMQ, enhanced conversion deduplication, and reduced the load on the website’s hosting server.

So, the real question is not whether client-side tracking works, but whether it provides you with enough accurate data to make informed and cognitive business decisions. As advertising platforms increasingly rely on machine learning to optimize campaign performance, providing them with the most complete and reliable data possible becomes even more important.

Server-side tracking does not require constant maintenance
----------------------------------------------------------

![Server-side tracking setup can operate without constant manual maintenance](https://stape.io/cdn-cgi/image/width=3840/https://cdn.stape.io/i/6a9a754939e41722199670.png)

It might seem that adding a server to your tracking setup requires additional attention and maintenance. In practice, however, things are much simpler. Once you finish the initial setup of the tags, data flows, and destinations, your server-side tracking setup can operate without constant manual maintenance.

Obviously, whenever you update your website, add new events, or analytics platforms change their requirements, you may need to adjust your tracking setup accordingly. However, these operations are not specific to server-side tracking; they are common maintenance tasks that apply to any tracking setup, including client-side tracking.

Stape makes ongoing server-side tracking maintenance even easier.

| **Area** | **What ongoing maintenance looks like** |
| --- | --- |
| [Server infrastructure](https://stape.io/gtm-server-hosting) | Managed by Stape |
| Infrastructure health and availability | Monitored 24/7 by the Stape SRE team |
| Tracking health | [Monitoring feature](https://stape.io/solutions/monitoring)<br> informs you when potential issues are detected |

This means that server infrastructure maintenance when switching to server-side tracking is taken off your hands. With Stape handling the server infrastructure, providing you with the tools to simplify configuration, and alerting you when potential issues are detected, you can focus on your marketing strategy and data analytics rather than worrying about the technical aspects.

Conclusion
----------

Server-side tracking is much more accessible for companies of different sizes, budgets, and technical backgrounds. It provides marketers with greater control over the tracked data that is sent to advertising platforms and analytics. This creates a much stronger foundation for accurate measurement and informed decision-making.

Stape is a great example of how server-side tracking can be implemented with minimal effort, combining managed server infrastructure with an extensive toolkit aimed at simplifying configuration, tag management, monitoring, and ongoing maintenance. At the same time, flexible plans allow you to start for free and scale your setup whenever your actual needs grow.

It is important to understand that server-side tracking is not a technology reserved for large businesses only. With the right configuration and tools, you can benefit from more reliable tracking no matter how big your company is or how much revenue it generates.
